title: Compact objects detect quasi-coherent derived isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] and choose any derived category [def-pc-derived-category], with its universe-$u$ coproducts [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-direct-sums]. For any morphism $g:A\to B$ of $D_{QCoh}(X)$, if $Hom(P,g):Hom(P,A)\to Hom(P,B)$ is bijective for every compact object $P$ [def-pc-compact-object], then $g$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09IS (perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh); compactness Tag 09M1; detection step of Tag 0A9R

proof.text: Noetherian X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply schemeDerivedQCoh_compactlyGenerated in the given Hom universe to obtain the inherited triangulated structure and a universe-u family E of compact objects whose coproduct is a weak generator. Use derivedQCohDirectSums X for the statement's coproduct instance; coproduct-existence instances are propositions, so the compact-generation witness supplies the same compactness and generation predicates. No change of derived model is needed.

Shifts preserve compactness. For K compact and integer n, the adjunction of shiftEquiv C n identifies each Hom(K[n],A_j) additively with Hom(K,A_j[-n]). Its inverse functor preserves coproducts. Naturality and the sigmaComparison isomorphism give a commutative square between the two direct-sum comparison maps, with horizontal additive equivalences, proving bijectivity for K[n]. The private compact_shift helper proves this directly from the compact-object definition and Mathlib's shift-equivalence, additive-adjunction and coproduct APIs.

Let g:A -> B satisfy the hypothesis. Shift adjunction identifies Hom(P,A[n]) -> Hom(P,B[n]) induced by g[n] with Hom(P[-n],A) -> Hom(P[-n],B) induced by g, conjugated by the two Hom equivalences. Since P[-n] is compact, this map is bijective. This is the proved hbijshift calculation.

Complete g to the distinguished triangle A -> B -> D -> A[1] in D_QCoh(X). For compact P and a:P -> D, its composite with the connecting map is zero: after g[1] it is zero by consecutive-composition vanishing, and injectivity of Hom(P,g[1]) cancels g[1]. Exactness at D (Triangle.coyoneda_exact₃, the rotated covariant exactness lemma) factors a through b:P -> B. Surjectivity of Hom(P,g) lifts b through A, so a=0 by g followed by B -> D being zero. Thus all maps from compact P to D vanish.

For each generator E_i and n, shift adjunction sends a:E_i -> D[n] to a map E_i[-n] -> D, which vanishes by the preceding step and compactness of shifts. The additive adjunction sends zero to zero, hence a=0. Coproduct extensionality therefore makes every map from the coproduct of E to any D[n] zero. If D were nonzero the weak-generator hypothesis would supply such a nonzero map, a contradiction. Thus D is zero. Apply Mathlib Triangle.isZero₃_iff_isIso₁ to the distinguished triangle to conclude IsIso g. Neither nonemptiness of the generator index nor of X is used.

Isomorphism detection by all compact objects in a compactly generated triangulated category

from.place: right adjoint commutes with direct sums: Proper perfect pushforward has compact isomorphism tests

lean.statement:
theorem derivedQCoh_compact_detection (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] :
    let _ : HasCoproducts.{u} (schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) := derivedQCohDirectSums X
    ∀ (A B : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) (g : A ⟶ B),
      (∀ P : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, IsCompactObject P →
        Function.Bijective (fun a : P ⟶ A ↦ a ≫ g)) → IsIso g
